fact_sheet.business_description: First Republic Bank provides relationship-based banking, residential lending, and wealth management services to affluent households [D01]. The institution's franchise value depends on its ability to maintain customer relationships while stabilizing its balance sheet amidst current liquidity challenges [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: Wealth Management: Generates fee income; not loss-absorbing capital [D06].
Residential Lending: Primary lending activity [D01], with $166.9bn in loans for FY2022 [D03].
Relationship Banking: Deposit-based franchise with $176.4bn in total deposits as of year-end 2022 [D02].
economics_vs_peers: Peer Comparison: JPMorgan Chase (ROE 14%) and others are not identical due to differences in funding franchises and business models [D06].
Growth: +12.9% deposit growth in 2022 [D02], compared to JPM (+5.8%) and Bank of America (+6.6%) [D06].
capital_structure: Borrowings: $15.279bn as of year-end 2022; increased emergency borrowing range of $20-$109bn (March 10-15) and $10bn FHLB borrowing [D03].
Preferred claims: Positioned ahead of common shareholders [D01, D05].
Liquidity Support: $30bn uninsured term deposit placement from eleven banks (120-day term) [D03, D04].
management_board_governance: Key Actors: First Republic management, eleven depositing banks, Treasury, Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC [D01, D07].
Prior activist history: Not in pack.
shareholder_base_and_liquidity: Average daily volume: Not in pack.
event_or_catalyst_evidence: Stabilization Mechanism: $30bn deposit placement by eleven banks announced March 16 [D01, D03].
Potential Catalysts: Deposit stability, disclosure of funding costs, and a durable balance-sheet solution [D07].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Funding Costs: High cost of emergency liquidity against low-yield assets [D05].
Capital Erosion: Potential for asset marks and expensive replacement funding to consume common equity value [D05].
Liquidity/Run Risk: Risk that customer balances continue to decline despite support [D03, D05].
deal_or_instrument_terms_if_any: $30bn uninsured term deposits from 11 banks; initial 120-day term at market rates [D03, D04].
recent_events: March 9-16, 2023: Significant reliance on Fed/FHLB borrowing [D03].
March 16, 2023: Announcement of $30bn deposit placement and dividend suspension [D03, D04].
third_point_context: 13F (Q4 2022): Disclosed holdings included PG&E, Colgate, Danaher, and Bath & Body Works [D08].
Stake in FRC: Not in pack.
missing_data: Current deposit retention rates, post-March 16 liquidity status, current fair-value tangible book equity, and Third Point's current position/basis in FRC.

final.memo:
First Republic Bank is a relationship-based lender currently caught in a systemic liquidity crisis that has necessitated an emergency $30 billion deposit injection from a consortium of major banks [D01, D03]. Despite the bank's historical franchise in wealth management and residential lending, the market is currently pricing in extreme existential risk as funding costs soar against a low-yield asset base [D01, D03, D05].

While the stock trades at 0.46x tangible book value, this metric is effectively meaningless without clarity on the fair-value marks of the underlying $166.9 billion loan portfolio [D03, D04, D05]. The reliance on high-cost emergency borrowings creates a negative carry scenario that threatens to erode the bank’s capital base rapidly [D05].

Management’s efforts are currently confined to stabilizing liquidity through regulatory and industry-supported intervention rather than driving long-term shareholder value [D01, D07]. With governance effectively ceded to the Fed, Treasury, and the depositing bank consortium, there is no actionable path for constructivist engagement to unlock a sum-of-the-parts recovery [D01, D07].

We see no edge in navigating this liquidity-constrained environment where the risk-reward is heavily skewed toward the downside [D03, D05]. Consequently, we are passing on the opportunity and will not participate in the common equity [D05].
